cards.text: The LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, and friend, this one's heavy. It's a law about what happens if a man's wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him with another man. And it's for when that would be hidden: no witness against her, and she wasn't caught in the act.

cards.question: This law also covers a husband who feels jealous and suspects his wife even though she has not defiled herself. True or false?
So the husband feels jealous, and there's no proof either way. Where does the law say he brings his wife?

cards.text: He brings barley flour for her too, a tenth of an ephah, with no oil poured over it and no frankincense on it. Friend, I have never left a cookie that plain in my LIFE.

cards.question: The barley flour gets no oil and no frankincense, because it's a grain offering for ___.

cards.text: And the text gives it a second name too: "an offering of memorial as a reminder of iniquity." Hold onto that one, friend, because this offering is coming back.
Now it all happens out in the open, friend. The priest brings the wife forward, has her stand before the LORD, and takes some holy water in a clay jar.

cards.question: The priest has holy water in a clay jar. What does he put into it?

cards.text: Picture this one slowly, friend. With the woman standing before the LORD, the priest lets down her hair and places the grain offering in her hands.

cards.question: While she holds the grain offering, the priest holds the bitter water that brings a ___.

cards.text: Now comes the oath, friend, and this is the serious part. The priest puts the woman under oath and speaks to her about two possibilities, starting with this one: no other man has slept with her, and she hasn't gone astray.

cards.question: If no other man has slept with her, what does the priest say about the bitter water?

answers.text: May she be immune to it
May she be healed by it
May she be forgiven by it

cards.text: And then the other side of the coin. If she has gone astray and lain with a man other than her husband, the priest has her swear under the oath of the curse.

cards.question: Under that oath, the priest says it's her husband who will make her an attested curse among her people. True or false?
Once the priest speaks the curse over her, what does the woman answer?

cards.text: Next the priest writes these curses on a scroll. Friend, I spent years under stacks of paper in that junk drawer, and I never saw paper do what this scroll does next.

cards.question: What does the priest do with the curses he wrote on the scroll?

answers.text: Washes them off into the bitter water
Burns the scroll on the altar
Reads them aloud to the camp

cards.text: Now it's time for the bitter water, friend, and the priest is to have her drink it. He also takes the grain offering from her hand, waves it before the LORD and brings it to the altar.

cards.question: At the altar, the priest burns the whole grain offering. True or false?

cards.text: Now the two outcomes, friend. Once she drinks it, if she has been unfaithful to her husband, the water brings bitter suffering: her belly swells, her thigh shrivels and she becomes accursed among her people.

cards.question: If the woman has not defiled herself and is clean, she will be unaffected and able to conceive children. True or false?

cards.text: Then the LORD puts a label on the whole thing, like the name on a cookie box: this is the law of jealousy. It's for when a wife goes astray, or when a feeling of jealousy comes over a husband and he suspects his wife.

cards.question: The woman stands before the LORD, and the ___ is to apply to her this entire law.
The law ends with a word about the husband. What does it say?

answers.text: He will be free from guilt
He will bring a ram of atonement
He will repay a fifth more

cards.text: And the very last line of the law: "but the woman shall bear her iniquity." That's the whole law of jealousy, friend, start to finish.
